programme.title: All Creatures Great & Small
programme.desc: Calum welcomes the new arrivals - one that bites and one that fits Siegfried's domestic requirement. James, meanwhile, receives an invitation to examine Lord Buttermere's new stallion.

programme.title: All Creatures Great & Small
programme.desc: Siegfried is saddened by the death of a young bull terrier and James has to deal with the Wains, a brother-sister team of farmers who have somewhat different approach to life and work.

programme.title: The Yorkshire Dales
programme.desc: Adventurer and explorer Paul Rose starts his journey in the town of Hawes where locals now run many of their own services, including the buses. Paul checks out why cycling is so popular in the Dales and tries to get to the top of the Buttertubs Pass.

programme.title: The Cult of ...
programme.desc: Unearthing the history and anecdotes behind cult Sunday night dramas looks at `All Creatures Great and Small'. With its mix of stunning countryside, eccentric characters and romance, the show formed a template for Sunday night television. Interviewees including Christopher Timothy, Peter Davison, Robert Hardy, Carol Drinkwater, Lynda Bellingham, John McGlynn, producer Bill Sellars and writer Johnny Byrne reveal the struggles behind the success.

programme.title: Walking With..
programme.desc: Comic Jim Moir explores a fascinating corner of the Kent coast as he walks down to Dungeness. Along the way he meets locals, explores military ruins and rides a steam train.

programme.title: Around the World in 80 Gardens
programme.desc: Monty Don is in South America, a continent twice the size of Europe and the home of more than 50,000 endemic plant species. In Rio de Janeiro, Monty visits the private garden of Brazil's most famous artist, Burle Marx. He views the ingenious floating gardens of the Amazon, and visits a crumbling estancia (ranch) in the windy Pampas. He ends his journey on the Pacific coast of Chile.

programme.title: Oak Tree: Nature's Greatest Survivor
programme.desc: George McGavin investigates the dramatic life of the oak tree, a species that makes extraordinary transformations as it meets the challenges of the four seasons.

programme.title: Banned! The Mary Whitehouse Story
programme.desc: A look back at Mary Whitehouse's campaigns, from her attacks on the BBC and boycotts against films like `Last Tango in Paris' to conflicts with feminists and the gay liberation movement, and her contention that pornography, made mainly by men for men, was not going to lead to greater happiness for society.

programme.title: Banned! The Mary Whitehouse Story
programme.desc: In the 1970s, Mary's battle with permissive society is hotting up, as suggestions that nothing should be censored gain currency. Nude actress Fiona Richmond publicly objects to Mary's `bullying' desire to stand in the way of her personal freedoms.

programme.title: Genius of the Ancient World
programme.desc: Bettany Hughes travels to China on the trail of Confucius, a great sage of Chinese history whose ideas have fundamentally shaped the country of his birth for around 2,500 years.

programme.title: The Story of Welsh Art
programme.desc: As the 20th century dawned, artists found radical new ways to depict Wales, pushing themselves to extremes and redefining what art could be.

programme.title: Fred Dibnah's Industrial Age
programme.desc: Beginning with a look at the early use of wind and water power, Fred traces the development of the steam engine and visits a man who has built a windmill in his own back garden. He then sets off in search of early beam engines that are still functioning today.

programme.title: Railways: The Making of a Nation
programme.desc: Historian Liz McIvor looks at how to organise a rail network in a country made up of separate local time zones and no recognised timetables. Before the railways, the country was divided and local time was proudly treasured.

programme.title: Britain's Lost Masterpieces
programme.desc: Pollok House is a country house right in the middle of a Glasgow city park, bordered on one side by the M77 and on the other side by the south side of Glasgow. It is owned by Glasgow City Council and looked after by the National Trust for Scotland.

programme.title: Call My Bluff

programme.title: Face the Music

programme.title: Arena
programme.desc: First of a two-part film profile of Orson Welles, looking at his life and career in theatre, radio and particularly film. With Jeanne Moreau, John Huston, Peter Bogdanovitch, Robert Wise, Charlton Heston, and a detailed interview with Welles himself. This part deals with his work up to `Touch of Evil'.

programme.title: Arena

programme.title: The Many Faces of...
programme.desc: A portrait of Ronnie Barker, a quiet dedicated actor who might have been a bank manager but went on to become one of the country's favourite comedy stars. Ben Elton, Michael Grade, David Renwick and Josephine Tewson are among friends and colleagues who remember his genius. One half of the Two Ronnies and the likeable convict Fletcher in `Porridge', Ronnie was also a prolific writer and admired actor in serious roles.

programme.title: Storyville
programme.desc: On 7 October 2023, Liat Beinin Atzili and her husband Aviv are kidnapped from their kibbutz as part of the Hamas-led attack on Israel. This film begins by following her parents as they attempt to secure the release of their daughter.

programme.title: The Covid Contracts: Follow the Money
programme.desc: This compelling documentary for the BAFTA-winning Exposure strand tells the untold story of how the UK Government went from having almost no stocks of personal protective equipment (PPE) to having more than could ever possibly be used, and how some companies with little or no track record in supplying PPE or medical tests were given massive contracts and made a killing from Covid - with access to hundreds of previously secret documents, e-mails and records, the film examines in forensic and comprehensive detail the decision-making which led to billions of pounds of wasted PPE being disposed of and the failure of the Government's costly test and trace programme to avoid a further lockdown. As the UK's Covid-19 inquiry - the most expensive in our history - rumbles on largely unnoticed, the film asks how this all happened and who was ultimately responsible.
